                                                           Abstract
          Multi-distribution learning (MDL), which seeks to learn a shared model that minimizes the
     worst-case risk across k distinct data distributions, has emerged as a unified framework in response
     to the evolving demand for robustness, fairness, multi-group collaboration, etc. Achieving data-
     efficient MDL necessitates adaptive sampling, also called on-demand sampling, throughout the
     learning process. However, there exist substantial gaps between the state-of-the-art upper and lower
     bounds on the optimal sample complexity. Focusing on a hypothesis class of Vapnik–Chervonenkis
     (VC) dimension d, we propose a novel algorithm that yields an ε-optimal randomized hypothesis
     with a sample complexity on the order of d+k ε2 (modulo log factor), matching the best-known lower
     bound. Our algorithmic ideas and theory are further extended to accommodate Rademacher classes.
     The proposed algorithms are oracle-efficient, which access the hypothesis class solely through an
     empirical risk minimization oracle. We also establish the necessity of randomization, revealing a
     large sample size barrier when only deterministic hypotheses are permitted. These findings resolve
     three open problems presented in COLT 2023 (i.e., Awasthi et al. (2023, Problems 1, 3 and 4)).1
     Keywords: multi-distribution learning; on-demand sampling; game dynamics; VC classes; Rademacher
     classes; oracle efficiency
